walkthrough: Goal: whatever interrupts me, nothing my hand drew is lost and the library is never half written.
Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape); draw a line with the Ink Pen; pinch the canvas larger and turn it a little.

Interrupted mid-stroke: I am drawing a second line when the screen turns off (or I press home, or a call comes). Back in the app: the line is there as far as I had drawn it, its end tapered as if I had lifted the pen there, and the canvas is at the zoom, place and angle I left it. Lifting or moving the pen afterwards changes nothing; one undo takes the line back.
Leaving mid-stroke: I am drawing a third line when I leave the app; the system closes it later. Opening OpenPaint again shows all three lines.

Killed mid-save: if the app is killed while it saves (a crash, the system ending it, an update installed), the artwork reopens exactly as it was saved last, never half of a save; a version kept when leaving is kept whole or not at all.

Low storage: when a save cannot be written (the storage full), the canvas keeps everything, a quiet pill says the artwork could not be saved, with Retry; the library on disk stays as it was saved last.

A failed upgrade: after an update, an artwork whose records the new version cannot upgrade (damaged by a bug or a broken write) stays in the gallery as it was, its picture marked Needs repair; tapping it says it needs repair, with OK; its options still save it as an OpenPaint file, so I can keep it until a fixed version opens it. Every other artwork opens and works.
